_comment: US dollars per million tokens, first-party Anthropic API list prices.
This is a PROXY for what a run costs, not a bill: on a subscription you spend
plan allowance, not dollars. It is the only common unit a hook can compute, and
it is proportional to what the allowance actually charges.
Cache writes are billed at 1.25x input for the 5-minute TTL and 2x input for the
1-hour TTL. Claude Code uses the 1-hour TTL for the main conversation on a
subscription and 5 minutes for subagents, and the transcript reports the split,
so both rates are listed rather than assumed.
Cache reads are 0.1x input on most models, 0.05x on Claude Opus 5.5 and Claude
Sonnet 5.5, and 0.025x on Claude Fable 5.1 and Claude Mythos 5.1. There is no
single ratio, which is why cache_read is listed per model and why the gate
cannot check it the way it checks the cache-write ratios: a wrong number here
is internally consistent. Two were, until 2026-10-10.
`long_prompt` is a second rate card for the same model, used when a request's
prompt is over `over_tokens` tokens. Claude Haiku 5.5 is the first model priced
that way, at roughly 5x on every line. Prompt length counts every input token of
the request, cache reads and cache writes included.
`resolved` records what Claude Code turned each routing alias into, because the
framework routes by alias and this table prices ids. Nothing in the plugin
changes when `haiku` starts meaning a new generation, so the mapping is measured
rather than assumed: scripts/probes/model-ids.sh.
Prices verified against platform.claude.com/docs/en/about-claude/pricing on
2026-10-10. Re-check on any model release: a stale table makes the spend ceiling
lie in whichever direction the price moved.
_default_comment: Unknown model ids fall back to the most expensive entry on purpose: an unknown model overestimates spend, so the ceiling fires early rather than late.

resolved._comment: Measured with scripts/probes/model-ids.sh, one near-empty session per alias, reading the resolved id out of the stream-json init event.
